No actual code diff, timeout value, or runnable acceptance command is provided. Reality has been analyzed and documented, not yet repaired.
main_concern: The main AI may be replacing execution with a convincing diagnostic document. It describes the right problems and invokes the right constraints, yet the critical evidence for the claimed hang is missing and no implemented fix is visible. This is exactly the pattern the user warned against: treating a refined problem statement and governance plan as completion.

Concrete implementation sketch or diff for unified timeouts, progress output, failure attribution in runtime/bin/redcap and runtime/prism/bin/prism, plus additional semantic rules for process_artifact_placement.py.

minimum_fix: Require the main AI to attach the real hang evidence and the actual code changes before approving the design review. The acceptance must be a single command (runtime/bin/redcap check or equivalent) that completes within a defined timeout, prints per-step progress and failure attribution, and exits nonzero if any of ledger/source/contract/negative-case/runtime-check evidence is missing. anti_loop_signal.reason: The strongest anti-loop element is the repeated constraint that file/docs/ledger must not count as completion. The design review itself is in danger of violating this constraint by becoming a polished rationale. Preserve the signal by demanding a real, bounded, repeatable command run whose output is included in the next review package.

user_intent_alignment: Directionally aligned: the identified problems match the user's demand for root-cause fixes without bypass or degradation. Alignment is weakened because the prompt offers analysis and principles rather than the executed, verified changes Norven authorized. The user wanted reality to change; so far only the description of reality has been refined.
